evidence: _poll_until_visible: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — search lag is expected mid-poll; keep polling until the deadline` / `pass` (lines 435-436)

ABSENCE: no test drives a client whose `search_issues` raises before later succeeding, so the keep-polling-after-transient-error contract is unasserted
test at line 478 uses `visible_at=60.0` with the default budget, an outcome reachable under a flat 2s poll too — ABSENCE: no test observes the growing/capped interval
advisory.finding: The retained mid-poll transient-error swallow (`except Exception ... pass` around `client.search_issues` for the summary fallback) is never exercised: `_EventuallyVisibleClient.search_issues` never raises, so no test verifies the poll keeps going (rather than aborting) when a search call fails transiently. A regression that let a mid-poll search exception escape and abort the poll would pass all three new tests.
merged_from: The exponential-backoff shape (1,2,4,8s capped) — the headline change replacing the flat 2s interval — is not distinguished by any assertion: `test_poll_until_visible_waits_out_slow_index_convergence` (visible_at=60, default 120s budget) would pass equally under the old flat-2s poll, and no test asserts the interval sequence or the `_MAX_INDEX_POLL_INTERVAL_S` cap.
scenarios: A refactor removes/narrows the mid-poll exception guard so a transient Jira search error propagates and aborts the poll early — undetected by the suite.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the fake client with a `raise_before` count so early `search_issues` calls raise, then assert `_poll_until_visible(...) is True` once simulated time passes the raise window and convergence.
